t.1.52.1: Thus addressed by Vasiṣṭha, O destroyer of foes, Śabalā, the wish-granting cow, provided the desired things to each and every one, just as each wished.
t.1.52.3: There were heaps of hot and rich boiled rice, like mountains, and delicious foods and soups, and likewise streams of curd.
t.1.52.2: Sweet sugarcane, and likewise parched grain, maireya liquors and the finest spirits, costly drinks, and foods of every kind, both high and low.
t.1.52.4: Vessels well filled with juices of many sweet flavors and likewise with ṣāḍava confections, and jaggery sweets as well, by the thousands.
t.1.52.6: Viśvāmitra too, the royal sage, then became delighted and well-nourished, that excellent king together with his inner apartments, and with his brāhmaṇas and family priests.
t.1.52.5: O Rāma, the whole army of Viśvāmitra, thronged with joyful and well-nourished people, was thoroughly satisfied, having been sated by Vasiṣṭha.
t.1.52.7: Then, honored together with his ministers, accompanied by his counselors and attended by his servants, he, filled with supreme joy, spoke these words to Vasiṣṭha.
t.1.52.8: O brahman, I have been honored and well received by you, who are yourself worthy of honor. Listen, O you who are skilled in speech: I shall speak a word to you.
t.1.52.9: Let Śabalā be given to me in exchange for a hundred thousand cows. For she is a jewel, O blessed one, and the king is the taker of jewels; therefore give Śabalā to me, for by dharma she is mine, O twice-born one.
t.1.52.10: Thus addressed by Viśvāmitra, the blessed Vasiṣṭha, best of sages, whose self was devoted to dharma, replied to the lord of the earth.
t.1.52.11: O king, I will not give Śabalā, not for a hundred thousand cows, nor even for hundreds of crores of cows, nor for heaps of silver.
t.1.52.12: O subduer of foes, I ought not to part with her from my side, for Śabalā is lasting for me, just as fame is for a self-possessed man.
t.1.52.14: The utterances of svāhā and vaṣaṭ, and likewise the various branches of knowledge: all this, O royal sage, depends upon her; of this there is no doubt.
t.1.52.13: On her depend the offerings to the gods and the offerings to the ancestors, and likewise the sustenance of life; on her too depend the agnihotra, the bali offering, and the homa as well.
t.1.52.15: In truth, this is my entire wealth, and she always brings me contentment. For many reasons, O king, I will not give Śabalā to you.
t.1.52.16: Thus addressed by Vasiṣṭha, Viśvāmitra, skilled in speech, then spoke words that were far more vehement still.
t.1.52.17: I give you fourteen thousand elephants with golden girths and neck ornaments, adorned with golden goads.
t.1.52.18: I will give you eight hundred golden chariots, adorned with little bells, each yoked with four white horses.
t.1.52.19: O you of excellent vows, I give you one thousand and ten horses, bred in renowned lands, born of noble stock and full of great vigor.
t.1.52.21: Thus addressed by the wise Viśvāmitra, the blessed one said, "O king, I will by no means give up Śabalā."
t.1.52.20: I will give a crore of cows, marked with many different colours and all in the prime of their age; let Śabalā be given to me.
t.1.52.22: This alone is my jewel, this alone is my wealth; this alone is my all, and this alone is my very life.
t.1.52.23: The new-moon and full-moon sacrifices, the sacrifices with ample priestly fees, and likewise the various rites: all this indeed she is to me, O king.
t.1.52.24: All my rites, O king, have her as their root; of this there is no doubt. What is the use of much idle talk? I will not give away the wish-yielding cow.
